paragraphs: Friend, let's talk about what just happened to David. He's marching with the Philistine army when he gets sent back, and he asks, "But what have I done?" (1 Samuel 29:8). Achish, king of Gath, tells him he has been upright and is "as pleasing in my sight as an angel of God" (1 Samuel 29:6, 9). And that good word still wasn't enough to keep David in that line.

So here's the lesson, baker. One person speaking well of you doesn't settle what everyone else decides. The Philistine commanders say David must not become their adversary in the battle, and they ask what better way he'd have to win back his master's favor than with the heads of their men (1 Samuel 29:4). I sat in the back of a junk drawer for years wondering what I did to land there, so I know how it feels to be sent away.

But watch where David ends up: heading back to the land of the Philistines (1 Samuel 29:11). I'm not going to guess what comes next. What I can tell you is that the story isn't over, and neither is yours. When you get sent back, keep your oven warm and keep walking, because this story is far from finished (1 Samuel 29:11).
